{
  "skills": [
    {
      "skill_id": "polar_apolar_balance_logd_core",
      "rules": [
        {
          "rule_id": "hetero_high_polarity_penalty",
          "conditions": {"hetero_atom_bin": "hetero_high"},
          "weight": -0.7,
          "rationale": "Dense N/O/S loading adds hydrogen-bonding and desolvation cost, the dominant negative driver of logD."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "hetero_low_carbon_rich_reward",
          "conditions": {"hetero_atom_bin": "hetero_low"},
          "weight": 0.75,
          "rationale": "Few polar atoms means mostly hydrocarbon surface, giving strong partitioning into the organic phase."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "halogen_high_polarizable_volume_reward",
          "conditions": {"halogen_bin": "halogen_high"},
          "weight": 0.55,
          "rationale": "Multiple halogens add polarizable apolar volume without hydrogen-bond donors, a classic logP enhancer."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "aromatic_high_hydrophobic_surface_reward",
          "conditions": {"aromatic_bin": "aromatic_high"},
          "weight": 0.3,
          "rationale": "Extended aromatic surface contributes hydrophobic contact area and raises measured lipophilicity."
        }
      ],
      "ridge": 1.5,
      "prior_scale": 0.35,
      "semantic_mass_start": 0.4,
      "semantic_mass_end": 0.15,
      "ucb_weight": 0.6,
      "gp_beta_start": 2.0,
      "gp_beta_end": 1.0,
      "gp_xi": 0.01,
      "confidence": 0.7,
      "hypothesis": "Lipophilicity tracks the polar/apolar balance: heteroatom load penalizes, halogen and aromatic apolar surface rewards. It may fail for ionizable or intramolecularly hydrogen-bonded molecules where logD departs from intrinsic polarity."
    },
    {
      "skill_id": "inverted_solubility_transfer_size_scaffold",
      "rules": [
        {
          "rule_id": "long_smiles_inverse_solubility_reward",
          "conditions": {"smiles_length_bin": "smiles_long"},
          "weight": 0.6,
          "rationale": "Source solubility fell sharply for long SMILES; solubility and logD anticorrelate, so large molecules should score high here."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "short_smiles_inverse_solubility_penalty",
          "conditions": {"smiles_length_bin": "smiles_short"},
          "weight": -0.55,
          "rationale": "Short SMILES were the most soluble source class, implying small polar fragments with low partition coefficients."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "ring_dense_scaffold_reward",
          "conditions": {"ring_token_bin": "ring_token_high"},
          "weight": 0.45,
          "rationale": "Rigid ring systems lower crystal-free aqueous solubility and present broad hydrophobic faces, favoring lipophilicity."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "branch_high_flexibility_downweight",
          "conditions": {"branch_bin": "branch_high"},
          "weight": -0.25,
          "rationale": "Deliberately weak: the rotatable-bond-to-branch transfer is uncertain, so flexible branching gets only a small penalty."
        }
      ],
      "ridge": 2.5,
      "prior_scale": 0.3,
      "semantic_mass_start": 0.5,
      "semantic_mass_end": 0.2,
      "ucb_weight": 0.45,
      "gp_beta_start": 2.5,
      "gp_beta_end": 1.2,
      "gp_xi": 0.03,
      "confidence": 0.55,
      "hypothesis": "Counter-hypothesis: source ESOL effects transfer with reversed sign because aqueous solubility anticorrelates with logD, so size and ring density become positive. It fails if long SMILES mainly encode appended polar functionality."
    }
  ],
  "selected_skill_id": "polar_apolar_balance_logd_core",
  "lesson": "Source evidence is solubility-signed, so it cannot be copied directly into a lipophilicity prior; the safest deployment rests on the mechanistic polar/apolar balance, while the sign-inverted size/scaffold transfer is the testable alternative.",
  "revision_summary": "Rewrote both skills so every conditions object maps one catalog field to one exact catalog value, removing the malformed list-pair conditions of the previous round. Skill one keeps the domain-knowledge polarity mechanism but replaces fragile two-condition interactions with cleaner single-field heteroatom, halogen and aromatic terms, boosting the hetero_low reward. Skill two is the explicit source-grounded counter-hypothesis: it applies the ESOL length effects with reversed sign (solubility anticorrelates with logD) and deliberately downweights the uncertain rotatable-bond-to-branch relation. Deployed the polarity skill as the more mechanistically robust prior."
}

rules.rationale: Dense N/O/S loading adds hydrogen-bonding and desolvation cost, the dominant negative driver of logD.
Few polar atoms means mostly hydrocarbon surface, giving strong partitioning into the organic phase.
Multiple halogens add polarizable apolar volume without hydrogen-bond donors, a classic logP enhancer.
Extended aromatic surface contributes hydrophobic contact area and raises measured lipophilicity.

skills.hypothesis: Lipophilicity tracks the polar/apolar balance: heteroatom load penalizes, halogen and aromatic apolar surface rewards. It may fail for ionizable or intramolecularly hydrogen-bonded molecules where logD departs from intrinsic polarity.
